E6-01.why: alternates bracket the error: child's (sing poss) / children (no poss) / children's (plural poss). The bracketing centres on a plural possessive, so children's is the residue. No Change unreadable without the stem, so partly guess.

E6-02.why: general rule picks one: 'since 1968' takes present perfect. C's past perfect has no later anchor, D changes meaning to a single 1968 event. Options-only rule, no passage needed.

E6-03.why: parallelism plus number singleton: C drops 'interpreting' and breaks the parallel, D is the only plural ('lectures') and so is the odd one out. Leaves B over No Change — guess between those two.

E6-04.why: redundancy ladder: B, C, D are the same content at increasing length (he was describing / he was at the time describing / he happened to be describing at that time). Shortest non-redundant rung wins; the ladder itself gave the answer.

E6-05.why: guess — 'having done' is a fragment-maker and 'have done' is an agreement distractor, but choosing 'had done' over No Change is a coin flip with no stem.

E6-06.why: option set alone decides it: D is the only option that both names what the essay does and states the specific gap ('never what makes the water rise and fall'), the standard key shape for a purpose question. A and C assert content, B is a thin negative. Concede-then-qualify tell.

E6-07.why: guess — bare Point A/B/C/D placement, nothing in the option set carries information.

E6-08.why: twin-pair elimination: A and D differ only in 'had put' vs 'put' and are otherwise identical semicolon clauses, so neither can be the unique key. That leaves B against No Change; B's comma reads as a legal non-independent opener.

E6-09.why: guess with a partial mechanism — compound subject kills B's singular 'has been', leaving were / have been / No Change; picking the past over the present perfect is unsupported without the passage's tense.

E6-10.why: C is the only option giving a redundancy rationale ('the opening sentence has already reported the two repaintings'), and self-referential redundancy reasoning is the usual key in this family. D is a factual-contradiction distractor, A asserts unsupported content. Partly guess against B.
